{"answer":"Logistic regression is a statistical model used for binary (or multinomial) classification. It models the probability that a given input belongs to a particular class as a logistic (sigmoid) function of a linear combination of the input features. Mathematically, for a binary outcome \(y\in\{0,1\}\) and feature vector \(\mathbf{x}\), the model estimates parameters \( oldsymbol{ eta}\) such that

\[
p(y=1\mid\mathbf{x}) =  rac{1}{1+\exp\! igl(-( eta_0 +  eta_1x_1 + \dots +  eta_kx_k) igr)}\,.
\]

The coefficients \( oldsymbol{ eta}\) are typically learned by maximizing the likelihood of the observed data (maximum‑likelihood estimation). Logistic regression is widely used because it provides a probabilistic interpretation, is easy to implement, and works well when the relationship between predictors and the log‑odds of the outcome is approximately linear.
"}
